findings.location: Decision, item 4 (“The grammar and the limits”)
findings.problem: The email grammar permits ASCII control characters other than a literal space, including tabs and line breaks. Such an address can satisfy the stated length, single-`@`, and nonempty-side rules, yet breaks the required one-line rendered approval/status sentence and permits output injection.
findings.suggestion: Define the email character set positively (or at minimum reject all ASCII control characters, whitespace, and line/paragraph separators) and require the complete stored identifier to be single-line printable text.

summary: The revised record addresses the prior findings, but its email grammar still allows multiline/control-character identities.
